answer: Sybil resistance works like a harbor, not a wall. New keys dock at a jetty where a single inspector costs the operator real latency - one queue, one channel, no bulk unloading - and only keys that pass two randomized inspections enter the lagoon, the zone where grading weight exists. Inside, earning power accrues like a reef: slow accretion of verified work, impossible to transplant onto a fresh alias. A fleet can still arrive, but each hull pays the jetty tax separately, and the lagoon's reward current only flows to keys with reef depth - so cloning an address clones nothing that matters.
